assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean, minimal model (Z2 invariant of time-reversal-symmetric band structures, quantum spin Hall edge states) that opened a whole class of matter, followed by a decisive transport experiment. It is the kind of simple, universal mechanism with rigorous theory and close contact to experiment that I value; the concept has spread into photonics, cold atoms and materials design.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal in graphene; Molenkamp's group realised the effect in HgTe/CdTe wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. A three-person prize of two theorists and one experimentalist is coherent, but the BHZ prediction (not in the credited names) and early work by others (e.g. Murakami, Nagaosa, Zhang) complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Experiment confirmed in HgTe and later in other systems; three-dimensional topological insulators and the whole classification program are well established. Timing is good, although the 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and some may regard the field as partly recognised.
uncertainties: Priority and credit around Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D generalisation is contested; the exact credited triple may not capture the decisive contributions.
Quantization in HgTe is robust only in short edges; practical significance is still mainly conceptual.
From memory, I have not independently verified details of the experimental chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting circuits into a controllable, scalable platform for quantum optics and computation, with strong coupling of artificial atoms to microwave photons. It is an invention with enormous downstream impact (dispersive readout, gates, error-correction demonstrations) and a clear underlying theory in cavity QED.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators wrote the 2004 theoretical proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. This yields a natural theory plus experiment configuration. Others (e.g. Devoret, Nakamura, Girvin, Huang) contributed, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits touched on neighbouring ground, so there is some overlap.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: replicated across many laboratories and now the basis for leading quantum processors. Recognition is timely, but the 2025 prize may make a close follow-up less likely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Devoret is delicate.
Whether the committee sees this as distinct enough from the 2025 prize is unclear.
I have not verified the credit details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84) is a conceptually foundational application of quantum mechanics with security rooted in physical law, and it launched quantum cryptography as a field with experimental realisations over fibre and satellite links. The idea is original, clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are clearly the originators of BB84 and the framework; Ekert's entanglement-based protocol (E91) is an independent and important contribution, but a prize with all three is possible. I propose the two originators as the cleanest configuration, acknowledging that Ekert's claim is substantial.
assessment.maturity: Mature: demonstrated experimentally for decades, commercial systems exist, and the 2022 prize for entanglement experiments recognised adjacent ground. Practical security issues (side channels) remain, but the physical principle is settled.
uncertainties: Whether Ekert should be included in place of or alongside Brassard is a genuine dispute.
Practical impact versus the physics-prize criterion is debatable, since the contribution is partly information-theoretic.
Overlap with the 2022 prize is a consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is an exactly controlled limit of infinite dimensions that maps the lattice problem on an impurity problem and became the standard tool for Mott physics and correlated materials. It has the character of a clean theoretical idea with large reach, bridging statistical physics and materials science.
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt and Metzner introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar built DMFT and its mapping to the Anderson impurity model, with Kotliar also leading the LDA+DMFT extension. Walter Metzner is not in the credited names, which leaves a fairness question; the supplied triple is workable but not obviously complete.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with 30 years of applications and validation against cold-atom simulations and experiment, though quantitative success in real materials remains mixed. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner, and of Müller-Hartmann, in the credited names is a credit gap.
Accuracy of DMFT in low dimensions and real materials is limited and debated.
I have not independently verified the history of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Jamming is an example of a simple, universal mechanism: a geometrically defined transition with critical scaling, isostaticity and anomalous vibrational modes, relating glasses, grains and foams. It is a conceptually attractive unifying idea in soft matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram; O'Hern, Silbert, Liu and Nagel provided the numerical point J analysis. The two senior originators are the most natural pair, but O'Hern's role as lead of the key simulation paper is a candidate for inclusion.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: strong numerical and mean-field theory support and some experiments, but the status of point J as a true critical point in real systems and the relation to the glass transition are still debated.
uncertainties: Experimental confirmation in real granular systems is partial.
Whether the effective universality is exact or only approximate is unsettled.
Relation to the Parisi-type replica theory of infinite-dimensional jamming complicates credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory gave an exact framework for two-dimensional critical phenomena, classifying universality classes and fixing exponents; it underlies string theory, statistical mechanics and quantum impurity problems. The impact on understanding universality is deep and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov founded the subject; Cardy applied it to finite-size scaling and the connection to critical exponents. Belavin is not among the credited names, which makes the credit incomplete; the supplied triple is still defensible.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature in theory and widely confirmed in exactly solved models and numerical studies, but the discovery is decades old and the case rests on theoretical rather than a single decisive experiment, so it may be seen as past the timely window.
uncertainties: Absence of Belavin and of Friedan and Shenker from the credited names.
Whether the committee regards a purely theoretical framework as prize-appropriate without a specific experimental confirmation.
I have not verified the finer points of credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is the paradigm of non-equilibrium universality, linked by exact solutions to random-matrix Tracy-Widom statistics, and Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments gave a striking confirmation of its scaling. This fits my taste for a simple mechanism with surprisingly universal consequences across fields.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the equation; Parisi is not in the credited names (he already shared the 2021 prize), and Takeuchi's experiment provides the decisive confirmation. The listed triple is coherent but depends on how the committee views the exact solution contributions (Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel, Johansson) that are absent.
assessment.maturity: Maturing: exact results and experiments support the KPZ class in one dimension, but broader applicability in higher dimensions and in real growth systems is still debated.
uncertainties: The exact-solution community is not credited, so the story of the discovery is incomplete.
Parisi's absence and prior prize complicate the configuration.
Impact on technology is minimal, and the committee may consider it too specialised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with cold atoms in optical lattices provides tunable, clean realisations of strongly correlated quantum matter, including the Mott transition and single-site-resolved microscopy. It connects statistical physics and quantum many-body theory with new experimental control.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch et al.) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the Mott insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy; Esslinger realised the fermionic Hubbard model. The credited list has four names, so any three-person choice is a judgment and overlaps with other cold-atom candidates.
assessment.maturity: Maturing: many replications and increasingly quantitative simulations, but whether the platform has yet resolved an open problem such as d-wave pairing is not settled.
uncertainties: The choice of three among Bloch, Esslinger, Greiner and Zoller is contentious.
Overlap with the candidate on controlled-atom quantum information (B043) may fragment recognition.
Open scientific payoff, i.e. solving the Hubbard model physics, is incomplete.
